# Mastering onboarding | Lauryn Isford (Head of Growth at Airtable)

## Transcript

Lenny Rachitsky (00:00:00):
Lauryn, what is the most common onboarding mistake you see?

Lauryn Isford (00:00:15):
Teams treat onboarding as a product tour. Onboarding is really about activation: getting a new user to experience the core value of the product as fast as possible. At Airtable we defined an activation metric based on whether a new user built a base and invited a collaborator in their first week. Activation predicted long-term retention far better than any tour completion rate.

Lenny Rachitsky (00:01:30):
How do you find the right activation metric?

Lauryn Isford (00:01:45):
Start from retention. Look at users who retained after a few months and work backwards to the early actions that best separate them from users who churned. Keep the metric simple enough that the whole team can rally around it, and run onboarding experiments against activation rather than clicks. Removing steps from signup often helped more than adding education.
